reader.requirement: At --std 85 the data-name-1 of a reference modification may carry qualifiers (data-names, a file-name) and 1985 subscripts (integer, integer data-name, index-name, each with relative +/- integer, multi-dimensional, over an ODO table) written before the modifier, as sender and receiver, while a 2002 arithmetic-expression subscript is refused.

edition-consulted.switches: subscript-arithmetic-expression-2002: refuses a subscript that is not a 1985 integer, data-name or index-name with optional +/- integer
the same construct: refuses a subscript data-name that is not an integer at 85

reader.edition-search: Grepped RefModBinder.cs, SubscriptBinder.cs, ReferenceResolver.cs for DialectLevel/ConstructRegistry/Constructs./CobolVersion; only the subscript-shape construct is consulted; qualification and the modifier bind the same at every edition.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: the subscripts data-name-1 may carry are narrower at 85 (an arithmetic-expression subscript is refused COBOL0900 at 85 and runs at 2002); qualification and the modifier itself do not differ
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f04_09 covers one-level qualification and single integer subscripts; not index-names, relative subscripts, multiple dimensions, file-name qualification, ODO tables, or the 85 subscript-shape refusal

reader.notes: A qualified or subscripted data-name-1 resolves through the one ReferenceResolver path and the modifier applies to the resolved element. The 85 subscript-shape gate fires on the subscript, not on the modifier.

refuter.evidence: rm-all.cob at 85: the Amendment 1 ALL subscript with a reference modifier, applied to each element (§1985:IV.4.3.8.4.4 GR3 a): FUNCTION MAX (TE (ALL) (2:1)) = Z, MIN = A, MAX (C (ALL, 2) (3:1)) = l over a 2-dimensional table; signed integer subscript TE (+2) (1:2) = BC; qualified data-name subscripts TE (K OF H) (3:2) = DE, TE (K OF G + 2) (1:1) = C, C (K IN H, K IN G) (2:2) = hi; receiving MOVE "XY" TO TE (K OF H - 1) (3:2) gives AZXY.
